 Order

This writ petition is filed seeking for following reliefs:
(a) Issue a writ of certiorari order or direction to declare that the Preliminary Notification no.LAO 1 SR5/8-89 dated 23.08.1988 issued under Section NC:
2023:KHC:45123 4(1) and published in Karnataka Gazette dated 01.09.1988 as per Annexure-B, and Final Notification issued under section 6(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 bearing no.RD/311/AQB/84 dated 25-09-1989 published in Karnataka Gazette dated 01.09.1989 as per Annexure-C, so far as petitioner land bearing Sy.no.18/3, 17/5, 19, 20/2 of Vajarahalli Village, Uttarahali Hobli, Bangalore South Taluk has lapsed in view of the Section 24(2) of the Act 30/2013 and also law declared by the Apex Court;
Ashwathanarayana vs State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65474302/
2 (b) Issue any appropriate writ, order or direction holding that acquisition proceedings have lapse and etc.

2. Sri A. Niranjan Kumar, advocate for Sri Shivananda H.G., learned counsel for petitioners submitted that petitioners' father was owner of land bearing Sy.no.17/5 measuring 1 acre 09 guntas,
Sy.no.18/3 measuring 2 acres 07 guntas, Sy.no.19 measuring 2 acres 21 guntas and Sy.no.20/2 measuring 0.06 guntas of Vajarahalli Village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bangalore South Taluk.
It was submitted that one Krishnappa had filed application claiming occupancy right against Munigerappa before Land Tribunal which by order dated 28.03.1979 was granted.
Said order was challenged by petitioners' father in W.P.nos.4295/1980 and 4790/1980.
Said writ petitions were allowed and matter remitted back to Land Tribunal.
Thereafter, Land Tribunal rejected claim for occupancy right.
Said order having been challenged in W.P.no.41880/2002 by brother of NC: 2023:KHC:45123 Krishnappa.

It was submitted that though said writ petition was allowed and matter remitted back to Land Tribunal, order insofar as rejection of occupancy rights of original tenant Krishnappa had attained finality.
In any case after remand, Land Tribunal had rejected claim by holding that land was not tenanted land.

3. It was submitted that said land was subject matter of acquisition for benefit of respondent no.3 - Society under Preliminary Notification dated 23.08.1988 at Annexure-B and Final Notification dated 25.09.1989 at Annexure-C.
It was submitted that respondent no.2 had passed General Award on 23.06.1990 as per Annexure-E.
However in said award, SLAO had taken note of alleged payments received by original tenant - Krishnappa and Seethamma from Society and deducted said amount from total award.

It was submitted that said deduction of compensation would not justifiable and therefore submitted that as an alternative prayer, in case, petitioners challenge to acquisition is rejected, order at Annexure-E insofar as deduction of amount may be clarified.

4. On other hand, Sri Yogesh D. Naik, learned Additional Government Advocate appearing for respondents NC: 2023:KHC:45123 no.1 and 2 and Sri K.L. Ashok, learned counsel for respondent no.3 sought to oppose writ petition.
It was submitted that admittedly, acquisition of petitioners land was as per Preliminary Notification dated 23.08.1988 and Final Notification dated 25.09.1989.

Therefore, present challenge filed in year 2015 after lapse of more than 35 years would be highly belated and therefore writ petition insofar as challenge to acquisition was liable to be dismissed on ground of delay and laches alone.
5. It was further submitted that challenge of acquisition by other land owners in W.P.no.4946/1990 ended in settlement.
Further, challenge by some other land owners in W.P.no.16858/2004 and connected matters came to be dismissed by this Court on 25.02.2014 as per Annexure-R6.

Thus,
acquisition in favour of respondent no.3 stood confirmed.

Insofar as deduction of amount received by Ramaiah as recorded at Annexure-E, petitioners had averred in para-8 of writ petition that aforementioned Ramaiah had taken signatures of petitioners on some papers and may have misused same, which would indicate that petitioners had knowledge about misuse by Ramaiah therefore no relief could be granted.
Ashwathanarayana vs State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65474302/
3 NC: 2023:KHC:45123 6.

Though, admittedly respondent no.3 has filed statement of objections, from perusal of same it is seen that writ petition filed by other land owners in W.P.no.16858/2004 and other connected matters, acquisition in favour of respondent no.3 - Society had been confirmed and therefore,
petitioners belated challenge was liable to be rejected.

7. Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.
8.
From above submission, it is seen that though petitioners challenge is against acquisition in favour of respondent no.3 - Society, same is highly belated.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation Limited v/s Chinthamaneni Narasimha Rao and Ors., reported in 2012 (12) SCC 797, has held that belated challenge against acquisition would not be tenable.

entities.text: Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation Limited v/s Chinthamaneni Narasimha Rao and Ors., reported in 2012 (12) SCC 797
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, acquisition of other lands in favour of respondent no.3 - Society under very same notification is confirmed by this Court in order passed at Annexure-R6.

Therefore,
petitioners would not be entitled for any indulgence at this belated stage.

However, insofar as alternate submission of learned counsel for petitioners about deduction of amount by NC:
2023:KHC:45123 respondent no.2 in Annexure-E General Award, SLAO at time of passing General Award is only required to assess total compensation payable in respect of lands acquired and cannot take note of payments made etc., by beneficiary to any one as if, he was deciding rival claims.
Observation in award to extent of denying compensation to extent of payment received by Krishnappa would not be justified.
Especially when payment is stated to be directly by Society and disputed.
Said aspect would have to be adjudicated only in case of rival claims under Section 30.
Therefore, award passed by Respondent no.2 - SLAO has to be read as granting total compensation of Rs.4,63,220/-.
With above observations, writ petition stands disposed of.
